name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+15) in rural Arizona
Incumbent Paul Gosar running with a cash advantage over $300K
No public general-election polling and no expert ratings to refine the picture
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 3%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Gosar: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and a clear fundraising edge, with markets and the absence of any rating listing the race as competitive both pointing the same way. Sterbinsky's modest fundraising is not enough to move the forecast materially.
model.watch: Any credible public polling or a major outside-spending intervention against Gosar would be the first sign the race is closer than the district's lean suggests.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Paul Gosar seeks another term in a rural Arizona district that leans heavily Republican, about fifteen points to the right of the country in recent elections. He enters the general election as a well-known incumbent with more than $300,000 on hand, while Democrat Dani Sterbinsky has raised about $354,000 but ends with limited cash and no reported outside support.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert race raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a three percent chance of winning. The forecast therefore rests on the district's partisan baseline, which points to a comfortable Gosar win, with uncertainty reflecting the thinness of available data rather than any sign of a genuine race.
